title: Yad Sarah: inhalers bought for neighbors in Jerusalem grew into more than a hundred lending branches

trailer.text: Uri Lupolianski founded the Yad Sarah organization with his wife Michal in 1976, and later served as mayor of Jerusalem.
In a harsh Jerusalem winter, people knocked on Uri Lupolianski's door in the evenings and asked whether he had an inhalation device.
He and his wife Michal bought a few inhalers to lend to the sick in their neighborhood.
Neighborhood residents began bringing the couple devices, walkers, crutches and wheelchairs.
In January 2026 the organization counted 7,500 volunteers in 127 branches across the country.

glance.label: Branches and volunteers
glance.value: 127 branches, 7,500 volunteers (January 2026, according to the organization)

stations.title: Knocks on the door in the evenings

paragraphs.text: Uri Lupolianski was born in Haifa in 1951.
He served in the Israel Defense Forces as a medic and taught at a religious school in Jerusalem.
In an interview he gave in 2021, he said that his family came to Jerusalem in a harsh winter.
On winter evenings people knocked on his door and asked whether he had an inhalation device, because the doctor had said that without a device the child must be taken to hospital immediately.
He said that he suggested to his wife that they buy two or three inhalation devices out of pocket money and lend them.
Neighborhood residents began bringing the couple devices, walkers, crutches and wheelchairs.
In 1976 Lupolianski and his wife Michal founded the Yad Sarah association.

stations.title: Named for whom, and with whose money

paragraphs.text: According to a 2013 article, his father retired and sold his shop in 1976, and gave his son enough money to begin the organization.
A 2025 book on the history of Yad Sarah, by Yaakov Wittenberg, says that the first center was set up on HaNevi'im Street in Jerusalem thanks to the father's donation.
More than 150 kinds of medical equipment are available for short-term loan, according to Friends of Yad Sarah.
Equipment may be borrowed from any branch, and a refundable deposit is requested.
A 2013 article states that the equipment is lent free of charge, and that a small deposit is usually required.
A 2021 Kan 11 report follows the route to the home.
The equipment goes out from Yad Sarah logistics centers across the country, arrives in special vehicles, and technicians assemble it and explain it in the patient's home.

According to one of the interviewees in the report, in the year before it aired there was a dramatic increase of hundreds of percent in the number of people who want to stay at home with equipment such as oxygen, a hospital bed and a lifting hoist.
The organization's 2009 promotional film stated that volunteers, guided by a few professional staff members, maintain and repair all the equipment.
According to the organization's website, in the workshops returned equipment is passed on for inspection, sterilization and repair before it goes to the next borrower.

stations.title: From one room to more than a hundred branches

paragraphs.text: A 2013 article wrote that Yad Sarah was founded in 1976 in one room.
According to Wittenberg's book, the first branch outside Jerusalem opened in 1977 in Haifa,
and within seven years there were 15 branches.
The organization's 2009 promotional film reported about 90 branches.
In 2013 an article described an organization of roughly 6,000 volunteers in more than a hundred branches, which it called the largest volunteer organization in Israel.
In January 2026 the organization counted 7,500 volunteers in 127 branches.
Budget Key ranks Yad Sarah third by number of volunteers among organizations active in the field of health and life-saving.
The association was registered with the Registrar of Associations on 24.6.1983.
Yad Sarah's reported annual turnover in 2024 was NIS 150,896,000.
According to Budget Key, this is the sixth-highest turnover among organizations active in the field.
According to the organization's website, most services are provided free of charge or at a subsidized price.

According to JTA in December 2008, American Friends of Yad Sarah had $1.5 million invested in 2006 with J. Ezra Merkin's Ascot Partners, a fund that lost all its assets in the Bernie Madoff scandal; Yad Sarah was still checking into the matter at the time.
The list of Israel Prize recipients for Tashnad (1994), as published by the awarding body, includes Yad Sarah in the field of special contribution to society and the state.
According to Makor Rishon, Lupolianski accepted the prize on behalf of the organization.

The Yad Sarah association and its founder Uri Lupolianski received the President's Award for Volunteerism, for the initiative and extensive activity in the field of rehabilitation and medical nursing care.
In 2005 Yad Sarah was recognized as an official advisor to the United Nations Economic and Social Council.
Lupolianski was elected to the Jerusalem City Council in 1989.
From 1993 to 2003 he served as deputy to Mayor Ehud Olmert.
In June 2003 he defeated Nir Barkat and was elected mayor.
He held the post until 2008, and was Jerusalem's first ultra-Orthodox mayor.
Wittenberg's book tells of a 72-year-old volunteer who collected a walker in Beersheba and traveled by bus to deliver it herself to an 87-year-old woman near Dimona.
The Kan 11 report features Hana, who is over ninety, and according to the transcript Eti cares for her.
The report travels with David to a woman who ordered a mattress, and says that in the past year he has been on the road a lot.
The report says that people know how they get into a hospital, but do not know how they get out of it.

stations.title: The difficult chapter: the Holyland affair

paragraphs.text: In April 2010 Lupolianski was arrested on suspicion of taking bribes to advance the Holyland construction project.
The Tel Aviv District Court convicted him in March 2014 of three bribery offenses.
According to the summary of the affair on the government website, the bribe money was given as donations to Yad Sarah, and an additional donation was given to a yeshiva run by his son.
Judge David Rozen wrote that Lupolianski did not take the money for himself and that he had devoted his life to acts of charity and kindness.
The same sentencing ruling found that the funds served to empower him and to increase his power and influence.
Rozen refrained from ordering forfeiture of the funds transferred to Yad Sarah and to the yeshiva.
The Supreme Court ruled at the end of 2015.
The conviction was upheld,
and the prison sentence was converted to six months of community service.
Lupolianski died in January 2026 at the age of 74.

disagreements.question: How exactly did it all begin?

versions.says: The founder himself, in a 2021 interview: people came and knocked on his door in the evenings and asked whether he had an inhalation device
A 2013 American article: a young high school teacher borrowed a vaporizer from a neighbor for a sick child. Word got out
Wittenberg's book, 2025: it all began with lending an inhalation device that was no longer needed in his home

disagreements.question: Whom is Yad Sarah named after?

versions.says: Makor Rishon, 2026: after Lupolianski's grandmother, who was murdered in the Holocaust
A 2013 article: after his paternal grandmother, Sarah
An investigation by Raviv Drucker, 2011: after his mother

disagreements.question: Does the state fund Yad Sarah?

versions.says: Friends of Yad Sarah: the budget is financed almost completely by donations, with no ongoing government assistance
Meir Meyer, vice chairman of Yad Sarah, in 2013: no government funding for a budget of 23 million dollars a year
Budget Key: NIS 27,163,734 in state funds over the last three years it covers, most of it in grants

disagreements.question: How much does Yad Sarah save the economy?

versions.says: The organization's promotional film, 2009: more than $250 million a year
Teva website, 2019: about $3 billion on hospitalization days

unknowns.text: Why the association was registered only in 1983, when activity began in 1976: the sources do not explain the gap.
How many devices were lent in the first years: the sources give only the founder's words about two or three devices.

claims.quote: The non-profit is named after Lupolianski’s paternal grandmother, Sarah, who had died in the Holocaust. The word “yad,” which literally means “hand,” signifies a remembrance or a memorial.

claims.text: תחקיר של רביב דרוקר מ-2011 כתב שהעמותה נקראת על שם אימו.
claims.quote: לא במקרה קיבלו אורי לופוליאנסקי והעמותה שהקים על שם אימו שרה, את פרס ישראל.

claims.text: ארגון הידידים כותב (לא מצאנו את שנת הפרסום) שהתקציב ממומן כמעט כולו מתרומות, יותר מ-70 אחוז מהן בישראל, וללא סיוע ממשלתי שוטף.
claims.quote: Yad Sarah’s annual operating budget is financed almost completely by donations, over 70 percent of which are raised within Israel. No ongoing government assistance is received.

claims.text: ב-2013 אמר מאיר מאייר, מתנדב וסגן יו״ר יד שרה, שאין מימון ממשלתי לתקציב של 23 מיליון דולר בשנה.
claims.quote: explains Meir Meyer, a volunteer and vice chairman of Yad Sarah as he led a tour of American journalists around the bustling, ultra-modern headquarters, located on Herzl Street, in the heart of Jerusalem.

claims.text: ב-2013 אמר מאיר מאייר, מתנדב וסגן יו״ר יד שרה, שאין מימון ממשלתי לתקציב של 23 מיליון דולר בשנה.
claims.quote: Meir notes that Yad Sarah receives no government funding to meet its $23 million a year operating budget; virtually all of its money comes from donations, 80 percent from within Israel.

claims.text: מפתח התקציב רושם לפי שלוש השנים האחרונות שהוא מכסה (לא מצאנו את שנת הפרסום) 27,163,734 ש״ח מכספי המדינה.
claims.quote: סך הכנסות הארגון מכספי המדינה בשלוש השנים האחרונות הוא ₪27,163,734, מתוכם ₪5,048 בהתקשרויות ו-₪27,158,686 בתמיכות.

claims.text: בסרט התדמית, שעלה ליוטיוב ב-2009, נאמר יותר מ-250 מיליון דולר בשנה.
claims.quote: חוסכת יד שרה לכלכלת המדינה יותר מ-250 מיליון דולר מדי שנה בהוצאות בריאות וסיבוב.

claims.text: כתבה מ-2013 הביאה אומדן של יותר מ-320 מיליון דולר, וכתבה אחרת מאותה שנה, 400 מיליון דולר בשנה.
claims.quote: In doing so, it’s estimated the organization saves the Israeli economy more than $320 million in hospital expenditures and long-term healthcare costs.

claims.text: מאמר באתר טבע מ-2019 כתב כ-3 מיליארד דולר על ימי אשפוז.
claims.quote: בהם מוצעים אלפי פריטי ציוד רפואי שיקומי לטיפול ביתי חיוני. כך חוסכת יד שרה לקופת המדינה כ-3 מיליארד דולר על ימי אשפוז.

claims.text: לפי JTA בדצמבר 2008, ארגון הידידים האמריקני של יד שרה החזיק ב-2006 השקעה של 1.5 מיליון דולר בקרן Ascot Partners של עזרא מרקין, שאיבדה את כל נכסיה בפרשת ברני מיידוף; יד שרה עדיין בדקה אז את העניין.
